name: prism-picker
title: Prism Picker
description: A hue picker built on optics: a white beam refracts through a glass prism (Snell's law, a Cauchy dispersion curve), a dial turns the prism, and the wavelength that leaves through a fixed exit slit is the colour, from the CIE 1931 observer through OKLCH to sRGB. UI SDK's slider in nanometres, painted additively on a canvas only when it changes, with setWavelength and setHue for agents.

[data-slot=\"prism-stage\"].background-image: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 58%, rgb(40 46 66 / 0.55), transparent 55%), linear-gradient(rgb(255 255 255 / 0.045) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.045) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(rgb(255 255 255 / 0.022) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.022) 1px, transparent 1px)

docs: `<PrismPicker label value|defaultValue onValueChange onColorChange disabled name labels>`. The value is a whole wavelength from 380 to 700 nm; `onColorChange` gets `{ hex, oklchHue, hslHue, wavelength }`, where the hex is the most saturated sRGB colour of that OKLCH hue (the red end is #ff0000), the same one the rays, the swatch and the readout show. The dial is UI SDK's Slider: arrows step 1 nm, Page Up and Down 10, Home and End go to the ends, and the value text is "470 nm, blue" (colour names in `labels.names`). A drag on the ring jumps the knob there; a drag on the prism turns it from where it was grabbed. Spectral colours only: magentas and purples have no wavelength, so `setHue` refuses them with why. The stage is a dark optical bench in every theme (the item's `css`); the card, readout and radius follow the theme.
